release_line_gate.activation_requirement: Keep M18-C limited to Nagi 0.1 browser acceptance infrastructure. Do not claim M18 acceptance until integrated guest evidence closes the required cases; do not implement M18 main/A/B, M19-PREP, or 0.2 product work.

blocker.summary: The safe base is the accepted M17 point and contains no integrated M18 browser API, so guest navigation, network, tabs, durable browser state, transfers, clipboard, and IME cannot be driven from this branch without importing other owners' unfinished production work. The M18-C feature-graph parser defect was fixed and follow-up hosted CI passed the actual target feature gate and M17 QEMU acceptance. Remaining blocker is guest-facing acceptance after the shared M18 API boundary is integrated. Local macOS Cargo graph inspection remains unavailable because third_party/cc-nagi was not fetched.
blocker.failure_log_summary: Hosted CI run 36409153587 at head 9cf9d40272fd29b4b8821620907b62f0fa2d3d35: `M18-C M17 feature-off acceptance and target report` failed with `M17 graph did not include expected nodes: nagi-init feature "m17-servo"`; the actual cargo tree command succeeded. Root cause: cargo tree does not print the requested root feature as a separate node; corrected by checking the selected nagi-init root package and nagi-albert presence while retaining the explicit --features m17-servo command argument. Hosted retry 36410949927 passed the feature gate, target build, and M17 QEMU acceptance with all CI jobs green; both M18-C artifacts were uploaded. Local cargo tree still reports `failed to read third_party/cc-nagi/Cargo.toml: No such file or directory`; earlier pinned fetch attempts could not populate the dependency due host toolchain/Apple xcrun architecture errors. Guest product cases remain SKIP-BLOCKED with owners in cases.json. M18-A CI run 36386094625 failed at remote web acceptance; M18-B run 36375495228 passed its current chrome acceptance. The M18 main integration checkout is separate and dirty, so it was not used as a base.

acceptance_criteria: A deterministic local HTTP/HTTPS fixture server covers direct pages, redirects, redirect loops, status errors, connection refusal, timeout, malformed responses, TLS verification, download, and upload.

Deterministic state fixture inputs exist for missing, empty, clean multi-tab, truncated, malformed, incompatible-version, partial-record, interrupted-write, and repeated-restore scenarios without defining or implementing the production storage API.
The 34-case report validates evidence identifiers, statuses, proof, ownership, blocked reasons, and overall PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL rules.
CI produces host and target acceptance reports and uploads them even when the corresponding focused checks fail or omit evidence.
The M17 target feature graph must prove M18-only browser features are absent; the M18-on graph remains integration-owned until a shared M18 target entry point exists.
No M18-A, M18-B, M18 main, M19-PREP, or 0.2 product implementation is added by this workstream.
All required guest-facing acceptance cases must pass on the integrated M18 implementation before this state can become PASS.
